From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 4 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: on-call entitlements & evidence (next steps)

Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a proposed next-steps list so we can qualify Greenridge's support-access requirements and map them to Redwood's controls.

Key points we heard on the call:
- Support needs JIT, time-limited access for live debugging of production customer requests (no standing broad permissions).
- Break-glass: an emergency path is required, with automated audit trails and a 2-person approval for elevated sessions.
- Residency: a subset of PII-derived logs must remain in us-east region for 7 years; aggregated telemetry can be global.
- Retention & deletion: customers require policy-level retention rules mapping to legal hold.

What I attached: redwood-support-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook draft), scoped-jit-matrix.xlsx (proposed RBAC/JIT matrix), demo-recording-20261004.mp4 (call recording).

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm by EOD Mon):
1) Confirm which Greenridge roles require read-only vs read-write vs escalation (see matrix).
2) Agree on break-glass approval flow (we propose 2 approvers: on-call SRE + Security manager).
3) Schedule a 90-min technical walk-through with your SREs next week to validate the JIT implementation.
4) Share any legal/retention exceptions we should model into retention rules.

If that aligns, I'll loop in Karthik and Monica to scope the runbook changes and produce evidence for your procurement review (SOC 2 artifact pointers, access logs examples).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Subject: Internal: proposed answers for Greenridge questions

Mateo — follow-up with proposed responses you can share with Alex. I started filling the runbook and attached the RBAC matrix. Notes below are written so they can be copied into the procurement packet.

1) Immutable audit record: Redwood can emit tamper-evident audit records for every elevated session. Implementation:
- Each JIT session is issued a UUID tied to a ticket ID (we can enforce ticket ID at session creation).
- Audit events (session_start, command_exec, file_access, session_end) are written to an append-only log (WORM-style) persisted in us-east S3 with object-lock enabled.
- Logs are signed and checksummed; we can export a signed bundle for attestation.

2) Residency & KMS: For Greenridge PII logs we will:
- Store PII audit logs and any object-level PII artifacts only in the designated us-east bucket.
- Block cross-region replication for that bucket using account-level policies.
- Optionally, integrate with Greenridge KMS (customer-managed key) so data is encrypted under your key; without that, Redwood-managed KMS will still encrypt at rest.

3) Retention & legal hold: retention policies are policy-driven in the console; we support legal-hold flags which prevent deletion until the hold is cleared. We can export a retention summary report for a given customer on request.

4) Break-glass approvals flow proposal:
- Step 1: Initiator creates a ticket and requests elevated session (include reason + ticket link).
- Step 2: Two approvers (on-call SRE + security approver) must approve via the console or an approver email link.
- Step 3: Elevated session is timeboxed (default 30 minutes) and automatically revoked; extension requires re-approval.
- Evidence: signed session bundle + video capture (optional) attached to the ticket.

Attachments included: scoped-jit-matrix.xlsx (matrix with role->permission mapping), runbook snippets in redwood-support-runbook-v1.pdf.

Flagging one operational question for procurement: if Greenridge requires video capture for every session we need to discuss storage cost/retention (video is large). Recommend we offer video as an opt-in for high-risk classes only.

I can be on the Tuesday 10–12 PST call with your SREs. Monica will prepare SOC2 artifact mapping (control IDs to evidence).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Please reply with attendee confirmations and whether you want video capture mandatory. Once we have that, I'll circulate the calendar invite + Drive folder with the artifacts.
